cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Here's the finished budget report. Just the title page: I've left room for contributions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The board meets in ten minutes. They need your figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It's the discussion edition. They can supply their figures directly, without reading mine first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair wants a recommendation, not a discussion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll add 'Approve' beneath the title. Finished decision edition. We've eliminated the discussion entirely.

mechanism: A approves successive completed editions of a report with no figures, turning requests for substantive work into permission for another minimal version.
confusable: D18 fakes expertise; D41 specifically relabels incomplete work as thoughtful completion, so the missing figures must stay explicit.
comparison: A board report uses discussion and decision labels, unlike the cupboard scene a physical kit and sample.
seedUse: Use D41-b title-only budget and requested recommendation, with S01 approving the definition of finished work rather than merely prefacing it.
